summary.text: Shekar Krishnan represents the 25th District on the New York City Council, which includes Jackson Heights, Elmhurst, East Elmhurst and Woodside in Queens.
His Council biography says he is the first Indian-American elected to the Council and now chairs the Committee on Oversight and Investigations.

paragraphs.text: Before his election, Krishnan was a civil rights lawyer fighting housing discrimination, a community activist in Jackson Heights and Elmhurst, and an attorney at Brooklyn Legal Services Corporation A.
He co-founded the legal services organization Communities Resist and led the Broadway Triangle litigation, which challenged a rezoning under the Fair Housing Act.

In his previous term he chaired the Committee on Parks and Recreation, and the biography says he passed legislation to decriminalize street vending and led a worker protection bill for Uber and Lyft drivers.
He is the son of immigrants from South India and is married to Zoe, an immigration public defender, with whom he has two children.
